annotations.blind_spot: One column going catastrophically wrong does NOT page — a vendor sending passenger_count=0 for every trip moves one column to a huge PSI and this stays silent. Deliberate: it is visible on the board and in the monthly memo, and A-9 needs no column to move at all. If a single-column catastrophe ever happens here, §8.3's paragraph was wrong and the split gets re-argued rather than the bar walked.
annotations.runbook: A drift alert is a request for a DECISION (retrain, re-scope, or accept), not a fault report. Read the per-column PSI and taxi_drift_unseen_share first: an unseen-category spike is a data-side event, a re-weighting is a world-side one. Nothing auto-retrains and nothing here can move @champion (M7 law 3).
annotations.summary: {{ $value }} monitored input columns are past PSI 0.10 for month {{ $labels.month }}
annotations.sustain: for 5m, and it is NOT F-041's mechanism. These are last-value gauges from a bulletin board, not a rate over a window that is empty at t=0, so the sustain's only job is to outlive a failed scrape of the gateway or a half-written push. 5m is 20 evaluations at 15s.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §8.3. The per-column bar 0.10 is 3.1x the highest distance a PROMOTED month sits at (0.0323 — dayofweek in July 2019, which is calendar arithmetic: five Mondays) and 7.3x the largest behavioural one (0.0137, PULocationID in August 2019). It is also the published PSI "investigate" convention, which matters for one reason: an on-call who did not write this document already has a prior for what 0.10 means, and a house-special 0.037 would be a number only its author could interpret. TWO columns rather than one because the champion's inputs are strongly correlated (hour<->dayofweek, PU<->DO) so a real world event moves several at once, while a single column moving alone is more consistent with a data-side artefact.

annotations.summary: Month {{ $labels.month }} holds {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of the reference's trips per day
annotations.sustain: for 5m, for A-8's reason: a last-value gauge, not a rate.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §8.4. The lowest ordinary observation in this repository is 0.7899 (August 2019 against the train reference), so 0.50 sits 29 percentage points below the quietest month a promoted champion was ever judged on. A summer dip is ~20%; halving is not a dip. A model quoting confidently into a market that has lost half its trips is quoting into a different market.

annotations.summary: The drift job has not reported for month {{ $labels.month }} in over 40 days
annotations.sustain: none, deliberately. The condition already contains a 40-day duration; adding a `for:` would mean 40 days plus five minutes, which reads like care and is noise.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §8.5. 3456000 seconds is 40 days: the cadence is monthly, so a month plus a week plus a weekend. One late run does not page; a stopped job does. The gateway has no expiry — a pushed metric persists until it is overwritten — so without this rule "drift is fine" and "the drift job died in March" render identically. The producer cannot be trusted to notice its own absence, which is why the guard is here AND in a type: push_metrics() REFUSES a payload with no taxi_drift_last_run_timestamp_seconds.

annotations.complement: `verify-m6` still asserts the holiday table's coverage. That catches the expiry BEFORE a rider meets it; this catches the rider who already did. Neither replaces the other.
annotations.summary: A quote was refused as past the holiday-table horizon in the last hour
annotations.sustain: for 1m, only to require the value to survive one re-scrape of the gateway. The condition itself is already "any refusal in an hour".
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §6. F-019 chose to REFUSE rather than degrade — a wrong quote nobody can see is wrong is worse than a countable failure with its fix in the error text — and the cost was that the refusal happens in the CLIENT, before a request exists, so no server counter moves. Measured at M6-S2: a past-horizon `make quote` left the infer counter at 22 -> 22. The client now pushes its own count, which is the metric source that did not exist until M7's pushgateway.

annotations.freshness: The `and on() (time() - ..._last_run_timestamp_seconds < 1800)` is not decoration. A pushed pair persists after its pusher dies and agrees with itself forever, so without this clause a dead pusher reads as a healthy service. 30 minutes.
annotations.honest_cut: M7-S3 landed the metric SOURCE, which is what F-035 said was missing. What runs the pusher on a cadence lands with M7-S4's scheduler. Until then `verify-m5` §2 remains the check that actually runs, at every gate, and asks the endpoint directly.
annotations.summary: The endpoint is serving version {{ $value }}, which is not the registry's @champion
annotations.sustain: for 2m, shorter than the ADOPTed 5m default and deliberately so. The other rules sustain to avoid paging for a transient — a slow scrape window, a self-heal in progress. This condition has no transient form: the wire and the registry either agree or they do not, and the state they are in is the state somebody left them in. The 2m is there only to let a re-deploy's own brief window close (M6-S4 measured a rollback's second move at 27.93 s, and a re-deploy at 0.5 s), not to wait out noise.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §6. F-032's shape: a rollback is THREE moves (alias, config line, re-deploy) and nothing enforced the middle one, so a half-finished rollback leaves the pointer and the wire disagreeing while every InferenceService condition still reads Ready — no restart, no event, no probe. Critical because the failure is silent by construction.

annotations.instrument_limit: F-043, measured at M6-S5 and argued in docs/slo_serving.md §2.2: THIS RULE READS AN IN-POD EXPORTER, AND ABOVE ~90% CPU THE POD CANNOT RELIABLY REPORT ON ITSELF. Under a throttled fraction of 0.9996 the predictor's /metrics went from 4 ms to 4.613 s with one scrape failing outright (the idle shadow, same job, stayed at 0.004 s) — which made this alert FIRE at T+349.3 s and then CLEAR ITSELF at T+514.3 s while the load was still running. A-1 going inactive during a saturation event carries no information. The instruments that hold are node-side (A-6, the kubelet's cAdvisor — it is what measured the 0.9996) and edge-side (A-2, ingress-nginx).
annotations.summary: More than 5% of quotes are slower than the 250 ms SLO target
annotations.sustain: for 5m, because a single slow scrape window is what a cold model load or one host hiccup looks like, and neither is a user-visible outage.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §3 SLO-L1. 250 ms is a bucket EDGE, so this is a count and not an interpolation. Observed at the SLO's stated shape (4 req/s, 60 s, concurrency 8, hazard mix): 258 of 259 infers within 250 ms, i.e. 0.4% beyond it against a 5% budget.

annotations.blind_spot: A ratio has no value when nobody is asking. This rule is blind on an idle service, which is exactly why A-5 exists and does not need traffic to fire.
annotations.summary: More than 10% of quote-route requests are 5xx at the edge, sustained
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §3 SLO-A1. Measured at the EDGE because when the predictor dies its exporter dies with it — mlserver cannot report its own absence.

annotations.summary: More than 1% of inference requests are being REJECTED as malformed (4xx)
annotations.sustain: for 2m, not 5m. A malformed body is a client-version or encoding defect; it does not self-heal, so the sustain window only has to outlast a probe or a single bad caller.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §3 SLO-R1. A 4xx here is the REQUEST's fault and is a working guard, not an outage — which is why it is separated from SLO-A1's error budget entirely rather than folded into it. F-030 is the worked example: ~1% of all riders got a 422 for a whole milestone because the client serialised NaN, and nothing anywhere said so.

annotations.summary: The predictor Deployment has had no available replica for 2 minutes
annotations.sustain: for 2m, not 5m. This is the rule that fires with NO traffic, so it is the only witness to an outage nobody is currently experiencing — waiting five minutes to say "there is no server" is four minutes of silence bought for nothing. 2m is chosen against the measured recoveries, not against the ADOPTed default.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §3 SLO-A1. 2m is 6.6x the longest healthy recovery this program has ever measured (18.24 s, the stop/start rehearsal), so a normal replacement cannot page and a pod that cannot come back does. One replica, no canary: this alert IS the outage.

annotations.summary: The predictor container has restarted more than twice in 15 minutes
annotations.sustain: for 0m deliberately — `increase(...[15m])` IS the window. Adding a `for:` on top would mean a flapping pod has to keep flapping after it has already been detected flapping.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §3. Steady state is 0 restarts (observed since M5-S2). Two is a coincidence; three inside a quarter hour is a loop, and each one costs a full outage because there is one replica.

annotations.summary: The predictor is spending >90% of CFS periods throttled — it is at its CPU ceiling
annotations.sustain: for 10m, because the honest response is "add a replica or raise the limit", which nobody should be paged for at 3am over a two-minute burst.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §3 SLO-L1's capacity note. At 0.79 the p50 is unchanged; at ~1.00 it is 6.4x worse with ZERO errors. This is the only signal that can tell those apart.

annotations.summary: A predictor pod's storage-initializer has not become ready for 3 minutes
annotations.sustain: for 3m. What the pair actually gives is a distinguishable SIGNATURE rather than an ordering: A-5 alone is "the replica is gone" (a kill, a stop, an eviction), A-5 THEN A-7 sixty seconds later is "the replacement cannot fetch its model" — the credential/prefix class. Gameday 1 got the second shape exactly and no other alert moved. Making A-7 arrive first would mean shortening it to ~1m, which is a threshold change argued from a number just measured; it is written up in docs/gameday_m6.md §3.1 as a recommendation and deliberately NOT taken here.
annotations.why: docs/slo_serving.md §3 SLO-A1. Two real classes land here and BOTH look like "the model is broken" when they are not: MinIO's built-in `readonly` policy omitting s3:ListBucket (a 403 on HeadBucket, M5-S2), and F-009's empty-prefix download that SUCCEEDS and leaves mlserver with no MLmodel. A healthy init takes seconds; 3m is a failure. MEASURED 2026-08-19 (Gameday 1, scenario 2 — the first of those two classes injected for real): this alert fires SIXTY SECONDS AFTER A-5, not before it. Both went pending together at T+30.1s; A-5 fired at T+150.2s on its 2m sustain and this one at T+210.2s on its 3m. The sentence that used to sit here claimed the opposite and was never anything but an inference from "a pod that never initialises never had a replica to lose" — true about the CAUSE, silent about the two `for:` windows underneath.
